notes: EPT (mayfly/stonefly/caddisfly) taxa richness; more sensitive taxa indicate better condition.
Benthic Shannon diversity; higher diversity indicates better condition.

NRSA benthic macroinvertebrate multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. EPA's Wadeable Streams Assessment MMI of six metrics scored per NARS-9 region, the same index in every survey cycle; EPA's own condition benchmarks are the published criterion it can be scored against.
Percent tolerant individuals; a higher share of pollution-tolerant taxa indicates worse condition.
Total benthic taxa richness; higher is better.
Chlorophyll a; higher indicates algal enrichment/eutrophication (worse).
Specific conductance; higher indicates ionic disturbance (worse).
Total nitrogen; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse). The total fraction, reported in every NRSA cycle, and the fraction published nitrogen criteria are written against.
pH degrades condition at BOTH extremes. Two-sided (optimum) curve: scored 1.0 across the reference interquartile core, falling in both tails.
Total phosphorus; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse).
Turbidity; higher indicates more suspended sediment (worse).

NRSA fish multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. Eight metrics per NARS-9 region, several adjusted for watershed area, scored from an electrofishing sample; sites sampled by seining carry no index.
Native fish taxa richness; higher is better.
Bankfull width-to-depth ratio; both over-widened (very high) and incised (very low) degrade condition. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.

Log relative bed stability; departure from the reference core in EITHER direction departs from reference (negative excess fines, positive an armored, sediment-starved bed, the classic below-impoundment failure). The pilot's rising direction scored armored beds 1.0 and left Sediment continuity blind to its textbook failure mode. Two-sided form is an owner decision at the adversarial review gate, 2026-08-21.
Log mean substrate diameter; coarser substrate generally better, but valley-type dependent.
Percent fast-water (riffle/run) habitat; more generally better for many biota. Ecoregion-dependent.
Percent sand and fines; higher indicates fine-sediment loading (worse).
Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.
Channel sinuosity; higher generally indicates a more natural planform.

Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.
Mean bankfull height; both incision (very high banks) and over-widening (very low) depart from reference. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.
Mid-channel canopy density; higher shading generally better for thermal/light regime.
Riparian canopy plus mid-layer plus ground cover; higher is better.
Percent embeddedness; higher means interstitial spaces filled with fines (worse).
Natural fish cover; higher is better.

Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.

Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).
Mean watershed elevation; physiographic scaling context. Predictor only.
Mean annual precipitation (1981-2010 normal); scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.
Mean annual runoff; scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.

bent_TOTLNTAX.notes: Total benthic taxa richness; higher is better.

chem_CHLA.notes: Chlorophyll a; higher indicates algal enrichment/eutrophication (worse).

chem_COND.caveat: Specific conductance carries natural carbonate geology as well as disturbance: a pristine stream in a calcareous valley can score low on this curve.
chem_COND.notes: Specific conductance; higher indicates ionic disturbance (worse).

chem_NTL.notes: Total nitrogen; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse). The total fraction, reported in every NRSA cycle, and the fraction published nitrogen criteria are written against.

chem_PH.caveat: pH carries natural geology (calcareous or naturally acidic waters) as well as disturbance, and a two-sided core narrower than measurement precision is noise rather than condition.
chem_PH.notes: pH degrades condition at BOTH extremes. Two-sided (optimum) curve: scored 1.0 across the reference interquartile core, falling in both tails.

chem_PTL.notes: Total phosphorus; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse).

chem_TURB.notes: Turbidity; higher indicates more suspended sediment (worse).

fish_MMI_FISH.notes: NRSA fish multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. Eight metrics per NARS-9 region, several adjusted for watershed area, scored from an electrofishing sample; sites sampled by seining carry no index.

fish_NAT_TOTLNTAX.notes: Native fish taxa richness; higher is better.

phab_BFWD_RAT.notes: Bankfull width-to-depth ratio; both over-widened (very high) and incised (very low) degrade condition. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.

phab_LRBS_use.notes: Log relative bed stability; departure from the reference core in EITHER direction departs from reference (negative excess fines, positive an armored, sediment-starved bed, the classic below-impoundment failure). The pilot's rising direction scored armored beds 1.0 and left Sediment continuity blind to its textbook failure mode. Two-sided form is an owner decision at the adversarial review gate, 2026-08-21.

phab_LSUB_DMM.notes: Log mean substrate diameter; coarser substrate generally better, but valley-type dependent.

phab_PCT_FAST.notes: Percent fast-water (riffle/run) habitat; more generally better for many biota. Ecoregion-dependent.

phab_PCT_SAFN.notes: Percent sand and fines; higher indicates fine-sediment loading (worse).

phab_RP100_cm.notes: Residual pool depth per 100 m; deeper residual pools generally better habitat.

phab_SINU.notes: Channel sinuosity; higher generally indicates a more natural planform.

phab_XBKA.notes: Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Direction resolved at the Northeastern Highlands review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21), consistent with the width-to-depth and bankfull-height treatment. low_tail flat added at the adversarial review gate (owner decision, 2026-08-21): a regraded or naturally gentle bank holds at the Functioning edge instead of being penalized, because the flat tail is not symmetric evidence of degradation and the framework's stated use is restoration evaluation.

phab_XBKF_H.notes: Mean bankfull height; both incision (very high banks) and over-widening (very low) depart from reference. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.

phab_XCDENMID.notes: Mid-channel canopy density; higher shading generally better for thermal/light regime.

phab_XCMGW.notes: Riparian canopy plus mid-layer plus ground cover; higher is better.

phab_XEMBED.notes: Percent embeddedness; higher means interstitial spaces filled with fines (worse).

phab_XFC_NAT.notes: Natural fish cover; higher is better.

bfiws.caveat: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.
bfiws.notes: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.

pctwet2019ws.caveat: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.
pctwet2019ws.notes: Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).

DrainageAreaClass.notes: Watershed drainage area class. Breakpoints 10 and 100 km2 are fixed constants.
DrainageAreaClass.rationale: Drainage area is the primary scaling variable for channel geometry, discharge and assemblage composition. 10 km2 separates headwaters from wadeable small streams; 100 km2 separates small streams from larger wadeable rivers. Both are conventional round-number breaks in NRSA and NHDPlus practice, not sample quantiles.

ChannelSlopeClass.notes: Reach channel slope class. Breakpoints 0.5 and 2 percent are fixed constants.
ChannelSlopeClass.rationale: Channel slope controls stream power, substrate sorting and channel type. 0.5 and 2 percent are the conventional low gradient, moderate and steep breaks used in Rosgen-family and Montgomery-Buffington channel typing. National median slope is near 0.13 percent, so this ladder is eligible in roughly half of L3 ecoregions; it is screened where it qualifies and excluded with a recorded reason where it does not.

ElevationClass.notes: Mean watershed elevation class. Breakpoints 300 and 1000 m are fixed constants.
ElevationClass.rationale: Elevation proxies thermal regime, precipitation phase and growing season length. 300 and 1000 m are conventional lowland, upland and montane breaks. Within a single ecoregion this often collapses to two populated classes, which the eligibility screen handles.

NhdSlopeClass.notes: NHDPlus V2 flowline slope. Adopted by the national scale analysis (rule STRAT-10).

elevws.notes: Mean watershed elevation; physiographic scaling context. Predictor only.

precip8110ws.notes: Mean annual precipitation (1981-2010 normal); scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.

runoffws.notes: Mean annual runoff; scaling/climate context, not a condition indicator. Predictor only.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 22 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 6 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 1 carries the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 4 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

referenceSupport.screen: least-disturbed-regional-v1 (relaxed tier, watershed agriculture at most 25 percent, the 25 percent floor)
referenceSupport.transferNote: 144 stations passing the regional least-disturbed screen (watershed agriculture up to 25 percent, the screen's floor, with the relaxed tier's other limits) from Level II 6.2 (Western Cordillera), 26 of them inside this ecoregion. Borrowed stations were matched to this ecoregion's streams on drainage area, channel slope, air temperature. Every station drains to this ecoregion's faunal province. Flagged transfer: the recovery test did not confirm this source for this ecoregion. In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough. The test found class agreement 0.50 of 18 evaluation regions, where two thirds over at least 4 regions is required; net optimism +0.01, where at most 0.05 is allowed. No source passed the validated acceptance criteria for this metric here, so the pool is used under the flagged-transfer rung as the narrowest comparable pool with at least the adequate floor of usable comparable stations that passes the sample, stability and comparability checks. The curve carries transfer risk unvalidated and its confidence is capped at 39; read the condition band with that limitation in mind.

transferValidation.why: In the recovery test the source's class calls did not agree with reference often enough.
